title: Why does soap make bubbles?
hook: Hi friends! Bath time is full of bubbles. Why does soap make bubbles?
answer: Water likes to hold itself tightly together, like friends holding hands. That is why a drop is round. Soap gets between the water friends and loosens their grip. Now the water can stretch into a very thin skin. Blow air into that skin and it puffs up into a bubble, like a tiny stretchy balloon.
wowFact: Here is a wow fact! A bubble is always round, even if you blow it through a square shape.
experiment: Try this! Ask a grown-up to help you mix a spoon of dish soap into a cup of water. Dip a paper straw in and blow gently. How big can your bubble grow?

onScreenText.experiment: Try it: soap, water and a straw

description: Bolt explains why soap turns plain water into bubbles and why every bubble ends up round. Then he mixes an easy bubble solution with a grown-up.
